15897856_d5424e2a.text: Glutamatergic MS-DBB neurons as a population display a highly heterogeneous set of firing patterns including fast-, cluster-, burst-, and slow-firing. Remarkably, a significant proportion exhibited fast-firing properties, prominent Ih, and rhythmic spontaneous firing at theta frequencies similar to those found in GABAergic MS-DBB neurons

15897856_5e7429ed.text: we found that some electrophysiological characteristics could be used to distinguish between glutamatergic and GABAergic MS- DBB neurons. Namely, the only firing pattern unique to glutamatergic neurons was cluster firing interspersed with subthreshold membrane oscillations

15897856_06a4dfb6.text: Some glutamatergic neurons exhibited burst firing that is distinct from the burst firing observed in GABAergic cells

15897856_091cecda.text: Subsets of glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons displayed the slow-firing pattern with broad action potentials similar to cholinergic MS-DBB neurons

15897856_33179aa6.text: cluster firing may be used as an electrophysiological marker for glutamatergic neurons in the MS-DBB

15897856_fc458e01.text: Glutamatergic MS-DBB neurons can spontaneously fire rhythmically at theta frequencies

15897856_0193c58c.text: Glutamatergic neurons in the hippocampus display highly heterogeneous electrophysiological properties and firing patterns (Huh et al., 2010)(Senova et al., 2020). These neurons can be classified into several distinct groups based on their firing characteristics, including fast-firing, cluster-firing, burst-firing, and slow-firing types (Huh et al., 2010)(Muller et al., 2017).

15897856_df7c382a.text: A particularly distinctive firing pattern unique to glutamatergic neurons is cluster firing, characterized by clusters of action potentials interspersed with subthreshold membrane oscillations (Huh et al., 2010)(Muller et al., 2017). This cluster firing pattern occurs at frequencies of 8-14 Hz and is found in approximately half of glutamatergic neurons (Senova et al., 2020).

15897856_d6af0d77.text: Notably, many glutamatergic neurons can fire rhythmically at theta frequencies and show prominent Ih currents (Huh et al., 2010)(Senova et al., 2020).
